examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: State whether the graph is directed and whether loops/parallel edges are allowed. Lists use Θ(V+E) space, with undirected edges normally represented twice. A matrix uses Θ(V²) space and gives constant-time edge lookup. Matrix powers count walks, not necessarily simple paths.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A simple undirected graph has 30 vertices and 75 edges. How many neighbour entries occur across all adjacency lists?

**Answer: 150.** Each edge {u,v} contributes v to u's list and u to v's list. The total is 2E=150 neighbour entries. The 30 list headers are not neighbour entries.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A matrix-based traversal can take Θ(V²) even when the list-based implementation takes Θ(V+E).

An adjacency matrix can be preferable for dense graphs or frequent edge-membership tests.
